locations.holds: the -76bps dividend bar and footnote 2 ($530m on-market, -10bps)
DRP satisfied in full on-market; participation rates

gold_answer_facts: The dividend reduced CET1 by 76bps on the Dec 25 -> Jun 26 walk, shown 'DRP neutralised'
The DRP was satisfied IN FULL by on-market share purchases — no new shares were issued
The interim-dividend DRP purchase was $530m, itself costing 10bps of CET1 (inside the 76)
DRP participation rates: 14.8% (2025 final) and 13.5% (2026 interim)
fact_check.answer: The 2026 interim dividend contributed to a 30 basis point decrease in CBA's CET1 ratio, which fell from 12.3% at December 2025 to 12.0% at June 2026 [ev-2, ev-3]. The Dividend Reinvestment Plan (DRP) component specifically reduced the CET1 ratio by 10 basis points due to the on-market purchase of $530 million of shares [ev-1, ev-9]. This DRP impact was part of the broader capital reduction driven by the payment of the 1H26 dividend, partially offset by capital generated from earnings [ev-4].

locations.holds: footnote 1 under the NII table — the only place the offset figures exist

gold_answer_facts: Average mortgage offset balances: $94,892m FY26; $84,123m FY25; $97,371m for the Jun 26 half vs $92,454m for the Dec 25 half
The balances are grossed up under accounting standards but netted down for calculating customer interest payments and the Group's NIM
Home loan average interest earning assets are therefore shown net of offsets
fact_check.answer: CBA's average mortgage offset balances were $94,892 million in FY26 and $84,123 million in FY25 (ev-1). These balances are netted against interest-earning assets for NIM calculation purposes, despite being grossed up under accounting standards (ev-2). This netting reduces the reported average interest-earning asset base, thereby inflating the reported Net Interest Margin compared to a gross basis. While spot offset balances were $94 billion in FY26 and $97 billion in FY25 (ev-3), the relevant metric for NIM impact is the annual average figure provided in the Profit Announcement.

footnote 1: underlying vs headline (+5.6% vs +5.8%) framing
the KPI table's CTI row (45.5 vs 45.7)

gold_answer_facts: Total restructuring and notable items: $170m (FY25 comparable framing: $130m implied by the benchmark's delta; FY25 items were domestic/NZ remediation and a Bankwest restructuring provision)
FY26 items: provisions for the settlement of legal proceedings in NZ; an additional goodwill payment to certain customers from ASIC's Better Banking review; domestic customer remediation
Underlying expense growth +5.6% vs headline +5.8% including these items
Headline CTI 45.5% (vs 45.7% FY25); the underlying CTI framing appears on the expense slide
fact_check.answer: CBA's FY26 restructuring and notable items total $170 million (cash basis), comprising NZ legal settlements, ASIC Better Banking goodwill payments, and domestic customer remediation [ev-1, ev-2]. These items are excluded from underlying metrics. Underlying operating expenses grew 6% to $13,585 million [ev-5], while headline operating expenses (including the $170m items) grew 5.8% [ev-9]. The underlying cost-to-income ratio increased by 30 basis points to 45.2% [ev-11], contrasting with a 30 bps decrease in the narrative which appears inconsistent with the table data [ev-6 vs ev-11]. The headline cost-to-income ratio improved by 20 basis points to 45.5% [ev-7].
